about: The enclosure control-loop target, in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real product: several bought-in parts that must be placed from a parts catalogue, openings and holes (subtraction), two printed bodies, and fit/access requirements judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match benchmarks/enclosure/requirements.md, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in Robin's words (keep-out heights, wall range, size limit) come from requirements.md section 3 and are provisional until Robin confirms them. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in benchmarks/enclosure/parts/*/part.json.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the board in, load path)

requests.title: Pico 2 CW keyer enclosure
requests.request: An enclosure for a 70 x 50 mm perfboard that will hold a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 CW radio keyer. The board has a mounting hole in each corner. The Pico 2 and two 3.5 mm aux jacks sit on the board, laid out long ways: the Pico's micro-USB port must be exposed through one short end of the enclosure and the two aux ports through the other short end, so cables can be plugged in with the lid on. The board must come out for service, so the enclosure is a base and a removable lid, printed on an FDM printer.
requests.request_verbatim: An enclosure for a perfboard that will hold a RPi pico2 CW Radio keyer with two aux ports on one side and the usb port exposed on the other (long ways). The perf board is 70x50mm.
requests.request_notes: Added to Robin's words, all from requirements.md section 3 or the photo: aux = 3.5 mm jacks (A5); corner mounting holes (photo); 'long ways' = ports on the two short ends (A1); base + removable lid (A10, A16); FDM printing (A11).

l1.text: The design shall place the Pico 2 and the two 3.5 mm jacks on the 70 x 50 mm board, from the parts catalogue, with the Pico's USB port facing one short (50 mm) end and both jacks facing the other short end, without the parts colliding or covering the corner holes, and shall declare that layout.
The 70 x 50 x 1.6 mm board shall fit inside the closed enclosure with at least 0.5 mm clearance to every printed surface, apart from where it rests on its supports.
The board shall rest on exactly four standoffs, one under each corner hole, each with a pilot hole for a screw through the board.

With the lid closed, no part of the enclosure shall come within 12 mm above the board's top surface or 4 mm below its underside, except the standoffs under the holes, and the Pico and jacks shall lie inside the enclosure.

With the lid closed, a micro-USB cable shall plug fully into the Pico through one opening in its end wall without touching the enclosure, and that opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.

With the lid closed, two 3.5 mm plugs shall plug fully into the two jacks at the same time through two openings in the opposite end wall without touching the enclosure, and each opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.
The enclosure shall be a base and a separate removable lid that locates on the base with a sliding fit and is held closed.
The closed enclosure shall have no openings other than the USB opening, the two jack openings and screw holes, and its walls, floor and lid shall be 2 to 4 mm thick.
The base and the lid shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports.
The closed enclosure shall be no larger than 90 x 70 x 35 mm, longest along the board's 70 mm side, and shall stand flat on a desk without tipping.
With the lid off, the populated board shall drop straight down onto its standoffs and every board screw shall be reachable with a screwdriver.

The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared board layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: subtraction: openings through walls (one rectangular USB opening, two round jack holes, lid screw holes) and blind pilot holes
interior placement: parts inside a parent's footprint at an inset (lid lip ring, bosses and standoffs at catalogue coordinates)
a shell / cavity primitive, or walls on a floor with the cavity known to the checks
two printable bodies (base and lid) with their own print orientation
parts catalogue: load part.json models (perfboard, Pico 2, headers, 3.5 mm jack, plugs) and place them by datums
envelope generation: keep-out volumes, plug insertion sweeps, screwdriver columns and the board install sweep
interference checks against external solids: clear_of, inside, aperture finding, gap, pitch, seating verification
optional: import vendor STEP/STL models and map their datums
